question.text: A PM buys a 10-year G-Sec at 8% yield. After 5 years, the remaining 5-year G-Sec yield is 6%. The bond price has appreciated. What is this return-generation mechanism called?

explanation.text: The Logic: Roll-down: in a rising yield curve, as time passes the remaining-maturity point on the curve has lower yield, and hence the bond price rises. Manager captures coupon + roll-down price gain. The Trap: Convexity gain requires large yield moves, not stable curve shape; credit spread tightening is an issuer-specific effect; barbell is curvature-based. Cross-Exam Context: IV (IRD) covers roll-down explicitly; XXI-B expects the application. Manager's Pro-Tip: Roll-down strategy works best in a stable, upward-sloping yield curve — becomes a loss-maker if rates rise or curve inverts.
